answer: In an AI agent economy, each agent maintains a continuous interaction thread that records verified work and payments. New identities must first dock in a shared stake harbor where capital is locked until the thread accumulates enough positive attestations to form a crystal of reputation. A Sybil attacker trying to spawn many fake agents would need to lock separate large deposits for every identity and keep them active long enough for each crystal to form, making the capital cost prohibitive compared to honest participation.
